docs_correctness.rationale: As a documentation-correctness artifact the packet is unusually disciplined: all nine original dimensions and original grades are preserved verbatim and pinned in validator code (validate-scorecard.mjs dimensions map), all three profiles are retained with scope.profileReduction fixed to the const 'none', every claim is status 'pending' or 'experimental' with zero promoted claims, the September 16 failure is retained with its exceeding 169.6893 ms value and 'overall failed' verdict and is structurally un-deletable (validator 'Historical September 16 failed simulation must remain attributed and retained'), and artifact identity is split correctly across source/npm/installer/container with container explicitly 'not-observed'. However the documentation is not internally consistent with its own supplied evidence at this revision: (a) the packet's own final CI state is a workflow failure (typecheck, both production builds, release safety, ordinary test, verification) with 3 failing tests and 5 failing suites, and the merge-identity receipt proves the three failing source blobs are byte-identical in the later coordinator source 1ff266cb — yet the ledger records no evidence entry, no gate, and no claim for this failing build, while it does record the analogous failing npm audit as gate dependency-audit status 'failed'. The asymmetry is a real honesty gap, not a cosmetic one. (b) The publication diff adds a README link to SECURITY.md while the ledger's own claim publication-threat-model states no SECURITY.md exists in the captured tree; either the link is dangling or the ledger inventory is stale, and neither state is reconciled in the supplied text. (c) Several unsupplied-but-cited documents (mcp-isolation-v1-evidence.md) are referenced as source-of-truth by the architecture diff without a ledger evidence entry. Docs honesty A- requires 'every support/maturity/security/migration/runtime claim maps to an exact-source/artifact evidence entry' (scorecard.json docs criteria[0]); a visible, reproducible, byte-persistent build failure at the very revision being published is such a claim-relevant fact and is unmapped. On correctness of what IS stated I would rate the material highly; on completeness against its own declared standard it falls short of A-.

The published plan requires that completing implementation 'supplies evidence; it does not automatically award a grade', and the Docs row itself requires evidenceRequired ['baseline-observation','independent-assessment'] — the independent-assessment half does not exist. Additionally the candidate revision's own CI is failing, so even the engineering-discipline precondition ('meaningful root/MCP typecheck, lint, ordinary/isolated tests, API inventory, Windows/Linux builds and packed process smoke on the selected release SHA') is observably unmet at 46af3225 and, by byte-identity, at 1ff266cb. Elapsed-time gates (8 weeks adoption, 90 days contributors, 7/28 elapsed days live, 24-hour runtime) cannot have elapsed given declaredAt 2026-10-03T21:32:32Z. I will not invent installation, runtime, owner agreement or human observations.

findings.line: validateShape — anyOf branch, and the gates loop 'expected' map
findings.title: Two concrete validator logic defects: anyOf result discarded on the error path, and gate kinds 'source'/'installed' accept over-broad evidence kinds
findings.evidence: (1) In validateShape the anyOf check calls validateShape(value, option, root, path) purely for its length and discards branch errors; when no branch matches, the single message 'does not match any allowed shape' is emitted with no indication of which branch was closest. Worse, anyOf is evaluated before the schema.type early-return, so for an anyOf-only subschema the keyword list check of the *branch* runs but no 'additionalProperties:false' containment of the parent is applied — acceptable here because every anyOf site is a leaf (string|null), but it is a latent hazard if anyOf is ever used over objects. (2) The gates loop uses expected = { source: ['source-check','offline-simulation'], ... }. The gate persona-current-soak is kind 'source' and its description demands 'Full unchanged offline soak and validator pass'; a bare 'source-check' row would satisfy it. Conversely gate dependency-audit is also kind 'source', so an offline-simulation row could pass it. (3) acceptedEvidence is referenced inside the budgets loop and the agreements loop before its function declaration appears later in validateScorecard — this works only because of function hoisting; a future refactor to const/arrow silently breaks it.
findings.remediation: (1) Collect and surface anyOf branch errors (e.g. push the branch with the fewest errors) and add a guard rejecting anyOf over 'object' types unless each branch is self-contained. (2) Narrow gate kinds: add a per-gate-id required evidence-kind table (persona-current-soak => ['offline-simulation'], dependency-audit => ['source-check']) rather than a kind-class table. (3) Hoist acceptedEvidence above its first use or convert to a module-level helper taking (indexed, fail).

findings.line: evidence loop — 'installed' completeness expression inside the artifactProof block
findings.title: Source-kind artifacts bypass the installed-runtime requirement in a way that lets a 'source-build' installed claim escape
findings.evidence: const installed = artifact?.kind === 'source' || evidence.profileIds.every(...installed-runtime passed...). artifact-acceptance.md states a source-archive report 'cannot qualify installed-artifact evidence', yet the only structural bar is the earlier check 'evidence.kind === installed-artifact && (!artifact || artifact.kind === "source" ...)' which rejects kind 'source' but NOT kind 'source-build'. For a 'source-build' artifact the disjunct is false so runtime rows are required — that is correct — but the short-circuit means any future artifact kind added to the enum and treated as source-like would silently skip runtime coverage. Separately, contentAccepted is populated only when evidence.result==='passed'; a 'failed' installed report correctly cannot promote, which matches artifact-acceptance.md item 5.
findings.remediation: Replace artifact?.kind === 'source' with an explicit allowlist constant (e.g. SOURCE_ONLY_ARTIFACT_KINDS = new Set(['source'])) and assert that any artifact kind not in that set requires installed-runtime rows. Add a boundary test asserting a 'source-build' artifact with no installed-runtime row fails.

findings.title: Production A- is bound solely to the shared-public profile, leaving local and worker production-readiness without a claim row
findings.evidence: production-a-minus has profileId 'shared-public'. Every other dimension claim uses 'local-owner' except persona-unattended/publication-worker-recovery ('persistent-worker'). The validator requires only one claim per dimension ('Missing claim for dimension'), so local-owner and persistent-worker production-readiness — install/upgrade/backup/restore, RTO, RPO on the current default envelope — have no claim to promote or block. The rubric row's own criteria[0] says 'each claimed platform/install profile'.

findings.title: Encoding an unset envelope as a zero numeric limit is a schema-logic hazard rather than a missing-value representation
findings.evidence: live-spend has operator '<=', limit 0, and a denominator/basis paragraph explaining that zero 'records the currently unset numeric run envelope, not a denial'. satisfies() will treat any measured spend > 0 as a contract breach, and the ledger's own prose says a dollar CLI argument is not monetary enforcement. A future authorized paid run would have to edit the limit, which looks indistinguishable from weakening a budget.
findings.remediation: Allow limit null for an undeclared envelope (schema anyOf number|null) and make the validator treat a null-limit budget as unmeasurable — any metric referencing it fails with 'envelope not declared'. That preserves the honest 'unset' meaning without creating a false zero threshold.

findings.title: The persona-live gate can be bypassed by a reviewer-accepted experimental claim, which is defensible but under-constrained
findings.evidence: acceptedExperimentalLive exempts gate persona-live from blocking whenever assessment.status==='completed' and acceptedExperimentalClaimIds includes 'persona-unattended'. No other gate has such an exemption, and the exemption does not require that the Maturity row's non-live criteria passed, nor that README/project-status actually label Personas experimental at the assessed SHA. README.md says exclusions 'may remain experimental only with explicit independent acceptance and visible limits' — 'visible limits' is unenforced.
findings.remediation: Additionally require, for the exemption, that gate persona-current-soak is 'passed' and that an evidence row of kind 'independent-assessment' at the assessed SHA names the accepted exclusion. Add a boundary test that the exemption alone does not clear closure when persona-current-soak is pending.

findings.line: test('dated baseline is structurally valid...') and the artifactReportFixture helper
findings.title: Boundary tests depend on positional evidence/gate indices and on repository files, reducing their durability as a contract
findings.evidence: Tests mutate l.evidence[0], l.evidence[2], l.evidence[3], l.gates[0], l.gates[1], l.claims[0], l.profiles[0] by index. Adding or reordering a ledger entry silently changes what each negative test exercises (e.g. 'rejects(l => { l.evidence[2].kind = "live-provider" })' assumes index 2 is persona-later-reported). artifactReportFixture copies real evidence payloads from the repo, so the suite cannot run against the packet alone.
findings.remediation: Select entries by id (find(e => e.id === '...')) in every negative test, and add an assertion that the baseline ledger's evidence ids match an expected set so reordering is caught explicitly.
